Here are the signs you might need a window replacement: Rising Home Energy Bills Older windows can let warm or cool air escape through cracks, forcing your heating and cooling system to work harder. Uncomfortable Rooms Window drafts can indicate poor insulation or thermal performance, making it harder to keep your home comfortable year-round. Manage Noise Control Aging windows often have failed seals, gaps or degrading frames that offer minimal sound buffering Window Operation is Faulty Difficulty opening or closing windows, sticking parts or pesky operational issues can be a sign that your window is nearing the end of its lifespan. Cosmetic Issues are More Apparent Chipped paint, tarnished hardware or material stripping can show a window’s age and outdate your home. Material Options A key decision in window replacement is choosing the right frame material. The most important part of choosing any window or door is understanding which type of material will work best for your home. Mountain West Window and Doors has a variety of Marvin window frames available in fiberglass, aluminum and wood. While replacement windows made from vinyl are less costly, low-maintenance and can be decent insulators, they tend to soften or sag from heat or direct sunlight and have few color selections. That means when the temperatures get high, vinyl windows begin to have problems fitting into their openings, making them difficult to close and compromising seals. Fiberglass replacement windows, on the other hand, have stronger structural performance, providing great insulation and premium durability. The fiberglass’s dimensional stability is very similar to window glass, making it an excellent choice for the intense climate of Arizona and Utah.
